memory_update.text: AMKR should remain the US-listed OSAT reference anchor for AI advanced-packaging capacity, but later layers must verify AI/HPC revenue materiality and customer commitments.
FORM is a higher-priority underfollowed test/probe-card candidate because its filings explicitly connect momentum to HBM chips used in generative AI.
KLIC is a promising but more cyclical advanced-packaging equipment candidate; key evidence gap is whether HBM/TCB orders become recurring and material.
COHU maps to the HBM inspection and AI processor test subnode; later work should separate genuine AI/HBM system revenue from broader semiconductor cycle recovery.
This pass did not fully cover materials such as underfill, thermal interface materials, ABF substrates, or US-listed photonics/optical packaging exceptions; those should be separate Layer 1B passes.

node: Advanced packaging, HBM integration, leading-edge foundry, and semiconductor equipment
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe around the AI advanced-packaging/HBM/test chokepoint using a two-lane funnel. One larger OSAT reference name is included as a mapping anchor, while the main discovery lane emphasizes less-obvious test, probe-card, handler, inspection, and bonding-equipment suppliers that sit one step below NVIDIA/AMD/TSMC/SK hynix/Micron/Samsung demand. These are research candidates only, not recommendations. Later layers must verify AI/HBM revenue materiality, customer concentration, cycle risk, and whether current valuation already prices the bottleneck.
